q: In Java, if a superclass has only a parameterised constructor, then every subclass constructor must:
options: Do nothing special; the compiler supplies default values
Explicitly call super(arguments) as its first statement
exp: No default superclass constructor exists, so the implicit super() would fail; an explicit super(args) call is needed.
g() is inherited from B but calls the virtual f(), which dispatches to D::f on a D object.

q: A C++ class becomes an abstract class when it:
options: Has at least one pure virtual function
exp: Any class with a pure virtual function cannot be instantiated and is abstract.

q: Why does the declaration List<int> fail to compile in Java?
options: Type arguments must be reference types, so Integer must be used
exp: Generics do not accept primitives; wrapper types such as Integer are used instead.

q: Which Thread method makes the calling thread wait until the thread on which it is invoked terminates?
exp: t.join() blocks the caller until t finishes.

q: Which UML diagram models the different states of an object during its life and the events causing transitions?
exp: State machine (state chart) diagrams show states and transitions of an object.

q: A friend function of a C++ class:
options: Is a member function of the class
Is not a member of the class but can access its private members
exp: Friendship grants access to private and protected members without making the function a member; it is not inherited.

q: Classes B and C both derive directly from class A. This type of inheritance is:
exp: Several classes inheriting from one base form hierarchical inheritance.

q: Which of the following cannot be overridden in Java?
exp: The final modifier forbids overriding.

q: Which of the following is a requirement for creating an immutable class in Java?
options: Declare fields private and final and provide no setters
Provide public setters for all fields
exp: Immutability requires that state cannot change after construction: private final fields and no mutators.

q: In C++, what happens when an exception is thrown and no matching catch handler is found?
options: A default handler prints the message and continues
std::terminate is called and the program ends abnormally
exp: An unhandled exception leads to std::terminate (which calls abort by default).

q: Objects created with the new operator in Java are allocated in the:
exp: All Java objects live on the heap; local primitive variables and references live on the thread stack.
Arrays are objects and b is another reference to the same array, so a[0] is 9.

q: The default copy constructor of a C++ class performs:
exp: The compiler-generated copy constructor copies each member, so pointer members are copied by address (shallow copy).

q: Which class is the root of the class hierarchy in Java?
exp: Every class implicitly extends java.lang.Object.

q:
Statement I: Method overloading is resolved at compile time.
Statement II: Method overriding is resolved at run time.
Which is correct?
exp: Overloads are chosen by the compiler from the signatures; overridden methods are chosen by the object's actual type at run time.

q: In Java, an interface can:
exp: An interface may extend any number of other interfaces.

q: Which STL container stores its elements in contiguous memory and supports random access with operator[]?
exp: vector stores elements contiguously like an array and supports O(1) indexing.
append gives abcd and reverse turns it into dcba.

q: The Open/Closed principle states that software entities should be:
options: Open for extension but closed for modification
Open for modification but closed for extension
Open to all users and closed to none
Closed to inheritance and open to composition
exp: New behaviour should be added by extending, not by editing existing, tested code.
Each add returns *this, so x becomes 2+3+4 = 9.

char is promoted to int (a promotion), which is preferred over conversion to double.

q: In Java, abstraction is achieved using:
exp: Abstract classes and interfaces declare what is done while hiding how it is done.

q: In Java, the throws clause is used to:
options: Declare in a method signature the exceptions it may pass to its caller
exp: throws lists exceptions a method may propagate; throw raises one.

q: Why is the Java main method declared static?
options: So the JVM can call it without creating an object of the class
So it can access private members of other classes
So it is inherited by subclasses
exp: The JVM invokes main before any object exists, so it must belong to the class.
1+2 is evaluated first as an int (3) and then appended: A3.

q: In C++, memory allocated with new int[10] must be released using:
exp: Array allocations made by new[] are released with delete[].

q: Java does not allow a class to extend more than one class mainly to avoid:
options: Ambiguity such as the diamond problem
exp: Two parents providing the same member would create ambiguity.

q: When a subclass defines a static method with the same signature as a static method in its superclass, this is called:
exp: Static methods are not overridden; the subclass method hides the superclass one.

q: Interfaces in C++ are typically implemented using:
options: Abstract classes whose member functions are all pure virtual
exp: C++ has no interface keyword; a class with only pure virtual functions serves as an interface.

q: Which statement about the Error class in Java (for example OutOfMemoryError) is correct?
options: It is a checked exception that must be declared
It is a subclass of Exception
It represents serious problems that applications are not expected to handle
exp: Errors are unchecked and indicate serious JVM or system level problems.

q: The synchronized keyword in Java is used to:
options: Allow only one thread at a time to execute a critical section guarded by the same lock
exp: synchronized provides mutual exclusion on an object's monitor.
